title: CLCON/344/2018 of Mahender Singh Vs R. Minakshi Sundaram

paras.text:
CLCON No.344 of 2018
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
(via Video Conferencing)
Mr. Naman Kamboj, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Pradeep Hariya, Standing Counsel for the
State of Uttarakhand.
A very peculiar situation has emerged in the
instant Contempt Petition, where the petitioner had
filed his contempt seeking an action against the
authorities for their disobedience of the judgment
passed by the Coordinate Bench of this Court on
30.07.2005, as rendered in Writ Petition No.730 of
2001 (M/S), Kisan Sewa Sahkari Samiti Ltd. vs.
Presiding Officer, Labour Court and subsequent
judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Apex on
09.08.2017, as passed in SLP No.10647 of 2010.
The contention of the counsel for the petitioner
is that despite of there being a direction issued by the
Coordinate Bench of this Court by the judgment dated
30.07.2005, the respondents are not granting him the
status of being a government servant under the
Assistant Registrar, Cooperative Societies, Haridwar
hence, alleges contempt.
On the other hand, the argument of learned
counsel for the respondents is that when the matter
travelled to the Hon'ble Apex Court, as against the
judgment of learned Single Judge dated 30.07.2005,
the Hon'ble Apex Court in the aforesaid SLP on
09.08.2017 has passed the following directions:-
"2. The civil appeals are, accordingly,
dismissed, however, leaving the questions of law
open.
No costs."
The argument of Mr. Pradeep Hairiya, the
learned Standing Counsel for the State is that infact,
when the Hon'ble Apex Court, had decided the SLP, it
had left open for the respondents that all questions of
law, would be open to be decided by the State. The
petitioner had preferred this contempt on 10.05.2018,

and contended that the direction contained therein has
not been complied. In response to it, the State has filed
a response affidavit of respondent no.4, under an
affidavit of Mr. Maan Singh Saini, the Assistant
Registrar, Vikas Bhawan, Roshnabad and particularly
the counsel for the respondents had drawn attention of
this Court to the contents of paragraphs 12 and 16 of
the response affidavit, which are quoted hereunder:-
"12. That vide letter dated 15.11.2018, 3
cheques of total Rs.30,43,304/- along with the
copy of salary bill were sent to him and on
16.11.2018 he received the same though under
protest. Payment has also been made against
these cheques by the bank. For kind perusal of
Hon'ble Court true/correct typed
version/photocopy of letter dated 15.11.2018
along with the receipt of petitioner marked on it
and the relevant page of passbook of district
cadre fund account are being annexed herewith
and marked as Annexure No.3 collectively and
respectively to this affidavit.
16. That the contents of para 4 of the
contempt petition are matter of record, hence
need no comments. However, it is submitted that
the petitioner had never been a Government
Servant. He was an employee of a Society and
remained in that capacity throughout his service.
His salary had never been drawn from
Government exchequer. Since the petitioner
being Technical Officer is not a Government
employee and hence could not be paid back
wages from Govt. exchequer. Honouring the
orders of Hon'ble court, it was decided that the
payment of the dues of the petitioner be made
from district cadre fund and accordingly
Member Secretary, District Administrative
Committee Primary Agriculture Cooperative
Societies/District Assistant Registrar,
Cooperative Societies, Haridwar was instructed
to pay his dues out of district cadre fund vide

letter dated 07.03.2018 and 11.10.2018. In
pursuance thereof vide letter dated 15.11.2018, 3
cheques of total Rs.30,43,304/- along with the
copy of salary bill were sent to him and on
16.11.2018 he received the same though under
protest. Payment has also been made against
these cheques by the bank. Since entire dues
have been released to the petitioner and further
that the petitioner has also been superannuated,
the order dated 09.08.2017 passed in writ
petition 730 (M/S) of 2001 stands complied with
in its true spirit."
In fact, if the averments made in para 12 of the
response affidavit are taken into consideration, the
respondents have come up with the case that by a letter
of 15.11.2018, a total amount of Rs. 33,43,304/-, as
payable towards the salary was sent to the petitioner
and it was received by him under protest. What he
contends to convey that in view of the pleadings raised
in para 12, the monetary benefits due to be paid have
already been extended and it has been received by the
petitioner, though under protest.
As far as, the direction issued by the Coordinate
Bench with regard to considering his status as to be
that of a government employee, the decision has been
taken by the State as referred in para 16, as referred
therein and the said decision has been supported by the
counsel for the State under the garb of the direction
issued by the Hon'ble Apex Court in its judgment of
09.08.2017 where all questions of law; have been left
open to be decided. In fact, owing to the aforesaid
stand taken in the response affidavit, this Court is of
the primafacie view, that the compliance as such has
been made by the respondents and if at all the
petitioner has any grievance alleging that it was not
compliance to the level of his satisfaction, as intended
by the judgment referred above, he has got his
remedies available under the U.P. Industrial Disputes
Act, 1947 itself by raising his contentions by filling an
execution or if the direction of considering his status,

as to be that of a government servant has not been
considered, then he has got the remedy under Section
11 (F) of drawing contempt proceedings before the
Labour Court itself, which has been vested with the
jurisdiction of contempt.
In view of the aforesaid reasoning, this contempt
petition is closed.
Notices issued to the respondents are discharged
with the following directions:
If the petitioner alleges that the compliance
narrated in paragraphs 12 and 16 of the response
affidavit, is not a compliance, he may invoke the
provision of Section 33(C)(2) and if he contends
that it is a non compliance of the direction issued
by the Coordinate Bench of this Court, then he
has got a remedy to enforce it by drawing
proceedings under Section 11(F) of U.P.
Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 07.09.2020
